reasons.plausibility: Graphene nanoplatelets in a metallic matrix at 500–1000 °C will likely react with the alloy (forming carbides) and degrade, making a stable graphene-reinforced grain-boundary network and a 25 % thermal-conductivity increase physically unsound.
reasons.testability: The proposed test compares thermal conductivity and structural integrity with/without 10 % graphene, but the falsification criterion mixes a quantitative threshold (15 %) with a vague 'compromise structural integrity' and does not specify how integrity is measured or what constitutes failure.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it ignores the well-known instability of carbon in transition-metal HEAs at high temperature, so pursuing it would waste resources on a fundamentally flawed concept.
